versions.provenance: International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics (FIGO) 2018 cervical cancer staging classification; licensed clinical reference.
versions.introduction: FIGO 2018 is the primary clinical and surgical staging system for carcinoma of the cervix uteri. Key 2018 updates allow imaging (MRI, PET-CT) and pathological findings to assign stage, divide Stage IB into three size categories (IB1 <=2 cm, IB2 >2-4 cm, IB3 >4 cm), and allocate pelvic node metastasis to Stage IIIC1 and para-aortic node metastasis to Stage IIIC2.

t.label: Carcinoma strictly confined to the cervix uteri (extension to corpus should be disregarded)
Microinvasive carcinoma diagnosed only by microscopy with maximum depth of invasion < 5 mm
Stromal invasion >= 3 mm and < 5 mm in depth
Clinically visible lesion confined to cervix or microscopic lesion >= 5 mm depth
Invasive carcinoma >= 5 mm depth and <= 2 cm in greatest dimension
Invasive carcinoma > 2 cm and <= 4 cm in greatest dimension
Invasive carcinoma > 4 cm in greatest dimension
Carcinoma invades beyond uterus, but not to lower third of vagina or pelvic wall
Involvement of upper two thirds of vagina without parametrial invasion (IIA1 <=4 cm, IIA2 >4 cm)
Parametrial invasion, but not out to the pelvic wall
Carcinoma involves lower third of vagina, extends to pelvic wall, causes hydronephrosis/non-functioning kidney, or involves regional lymph nodes
Involvement of lower third of vagina, no extension to pelvic wall
Extension to pelvic wall, or hydronephrosis / non-functioning kidney
Carcinoma extends beyond the true pelvis or has clinically involved mucosa of bladder or rectum

n.label: Pelvic lymph node metastasis only (r=imaging, p=pathology)

m.label: Spread to adjacent pelvic organs (biopsy-proven mucosa of bladder or rectum)
Spread to distant organs (lung, liver, bone, non-regional distant nodes)

stageGroups.basis: Cone biopsy with negative margins or simple hysterectomy (if fertility not desired).
Modified radical hysterectomy + pelvic lymph node dissection or conization.
Radical hysterectomy + bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy or fertility-sparing radical trachelectomy.
Radical hysterectomy or definitive chemoradiation (EBRT + concurrent cisplatin + brachytherapy).
Definitive concurrent chemoradiation with image-guided adaptive brachytherapy (IGABT).
Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (cisplatin) + brachytherapy; surgery contraindicated.
Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy with pelvic nodal boost + brachytherapy.
Definitive chemoradiotherapy or pelvic exenteration in selected cases.
Systemic therapy: Pembrolizumab + Chemotherapy (Paclitaxel + Cisplatin/Carboplatin) +/- Bevacizumab (if PD-L1 CPS >=1).

versions.regionalNodes: Pelvic nodes (paracervical, obturator, internal iliac, external iliac, common iliac, presacral, lateral sacral) and Para-aortic nodes.
versions.histologicGrade: Grade 1 (well differentiated), Grade 2 (moderately differentiated), Grade 3 (poorly differentiated).
versions.histopathologicTypes: Squamous cell carcinoma (70-80%), Adenocarcinoma (20-25%), Adenosquamous carcinoma, Neuroendocrine carcinoma.
prognosticFactors: Pelvic and para-aortic lymph node status (strongest prognostic factor)
Depth of stromal invasion and lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI - Sedlis criteria for adjuvant RT)
